messages:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's SDK shim rollout we started seeing duplicated telemetry for route attribution in the console. :confused:
ajay: I saw that spike too. Looks like some requests show both old header and new header being recorded.
maria: Yep. Example from access logs: 
```
{"time":"2026-03-20T09:12:34Z","headers":{
  "X-Redwood-Route":"tenant-42/priorityA",
  "X-Rdw-RouteHint":"priorityA"
}}
```
That ends up creating two route attribution traces in ingestion.
kelly: Are we double-emitting from the SDK, or is the ingestion pipeline dedup failing?
ajay: Quick triage — the SDK shim intentionally writes the new `X-Rdw-RouteHint` while preserving `X-Redwood-Route` for backward compat. The server ingestion had a dedup rule keyed on header name, not semantic value, so both get counted.
maria: Right — and console dashboards aggregate by "route tag" which picks whichever header it sees first, so we get split counts.
sam: Minimal mitigation: ingestion can normalize headers to a canonical route id before incrementing metrics. I can throw a small hotfix that prefers `X-Rdw-RouteHint` when present. Want me to ship?
kelly: Do it, but we need to communicate to SDK teams — this is a transient inconsistency but could affect billing/alerts.
ajay: Adding notes: 
- Hotfix in ingestion to coalesce headers (prefer new, fallback to old)
- One-week backfill to reconcile counts for last 48h (post-shim)
- SDK change: add opt-in flag `REDWOOD_SHIM_STRICT=false` for canary customers who want both headers removed slowly
maria: For the backfill we'll need raw events export. ops-bot, can you queue a raw export job for 2026-03-19 00:00 UTC -> 2026-03-21 00:00 UTC?
ops-bot: scheduled export job eps-20260321-01 created, ETA 45m.
sam: For the ingestion patch, here's the naive pseudo-fix: 
```
// ingestion header normalization
route = headers.get("X-Rdw-RouteHint") || headers.get("X-Redwood-Route");
if (route) emitMetric("route.request", {route});
```
It should prevent double counting.
kelly: Good. Also add a dashboard tile that shows "header-split ratio" (requests with both headers / requests with any header) so we can watch the migration.
ajay: Agreed. Also SDK owners: can we add telemetry that emits a single `route_canonical` field to the request body so downstream is robust even if headers are added/stripped by proxies?
maria: That's the long-term plan. For immediate next steps: 
1) sam deploy ingestion-button hotfix (canary to eu-west-1) — sam
2) ops run export and hand to analytics for backfill — ops-bot/kelly
3) ajay to add SDK env flag and docs for customers — ajay
4) devex to add dashboard tile + alert tweak — kelly
I'll post short status update to #product and #support once hotfix is live.
sam: rolling the canary now. will post deploy id.
(10m later)
sam: canary merged, no anomalies in 10m window. :thumbsup:
ajay: I'll open a tiny follow-up PR to add `REDWOOD_SHIM_STRICT` and a migration note in CHANGELOG.
kelly: Thanks. Maria, when ops backfill finishes can you coordinate reconciled numbers with billing for any customers in the affected bucket? We should be proactive.
maria: Yup. I'll draft an internal note.
ajay: One more edge case — some internal proxies rewrite header casing which caused the SDK to emit both `x-rdw-routehint` and `X-Rdw-RouteHint`. Ingestion needs to canonicalize case-insensitively. Verified in logs.
sam: fixed in hotfix: we lowercase header names before lookup.
maria: Great. I'll follow up in ~2h with final numbers and a short blurb for #support. Thanks all.
